verses.1: And while he was in one place, praying, someone from his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
verses.2: And he said to them, “When you pray, say, ‘Lord, make your name holy.’ Then come, for your kingdom is here.”
verses.3: Give us our bread, the one we can eat, every day.
verses.4: And may the heavens take away our sins from us. For they will indeed bring us back to what we owe them. And do not tempt us into temptation.
verses.5: And he said to them, “Who among you will befriend him and go to him in the middle of the night and say to him, ‘Friend, please give me three pieces of bread.’”
verses.6: Since my friend came to me on the way here, I don’t know what to give him.
verses.7: Then he replied from behind: “Do not take anything from me. The door is already closed, and my children are with me in the cellar. I cannot get up and leave with you.”
verses.8: I say to you, even if he doesn’t give him any gifts because he’s his friend, still, out of gratitude for his kindness, he should give him whatever he needs.
verses.9: I say to you, ask for it, and it will be given to you. Seek it, and you will find it. Knock on the door, and it will be opened for you.
verses.10: For every petitioner, something is granted; those who ask for something will find it. And when it’s closed, it will be opened.
verses.11: And which of you will ask their father for fish? And instead of fish, will they give them worms to eat?
verses.12: And if he asks for it, will he give him a scorpion in return?
verses.13: If you, who are evil people, know how to give good gifts to your children, then how much more will the Father in heaven give his holy spirit to those who ask for it.
verses.14: And when the demon left, the dumb man spoke. The crowd was amazed.
verses.15: And some of them said, “In Belzebub, the ruler of demons, the demons are sent out.”
verses.16: But others tried to find a sign from heaven.
verses.17: And he knew their thoughts, and he said to them: “All kingdoms that are divided among themselves will become empty and barren; each kingdom will fall apart from the others.”
verses.18: And even if Satan himself is divided within himself, how can his kingdom then remain stable? For you say that in Bethlehem, he sends out demons.
verses.19: But if I expel the demons from Belzebub, where will your sons be able to do it? For that reason, they will become your enemies.
verses.20: And if I cast out the demons in the rod of God, then the kingdom of God will indeed come upon you.
verses.21: When the strong and armored warrior guards his own palace, then he is in peace.
verses.22: But if someone stronger than him were to come along and defeat him, he would give up his armor and surrender. He would also hand over his weapons.
verses.23: He who isn’t with me is also lost in my absence, and he who doesn’t join me will also be lost.
verses.24: When the impure breath exits from a person, it seeks refuge in dry places in search of peace. But when it cannot find such a place, it says, “I will return to my home from where I came.”
verses.25: And when he came, he found her dressed and adorned.
verses.26: Then it absorbs seven more evil spirits of its own kind. After that, it settles there and becomes the “last part” of man, created by those first spirits.
verses.27: While he was speaking these things, a woman from the crowd spoke to him. She said, “Makaria is a disease that causes you to tremble and also affects those whom you love.”
verses.28: And he said, “Menon, those who listen to the words of God and keep them are truly blessed.”
verses.29: But when the crowd became angry, he began to speak: “This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign from God. But it will not be given to it a sign unless it receives the sign of Jonah.”
verses.30: For just as Ion became a sign to the Neveites, so too will the son of man be of the same nature.
verses.31: The Queen of the North will rise up in judgment along with the men of her lineage. She will judge them for having heard the wisdom of Solomon from beyond the borders of the land. And indeed, Solomon was far more wise than those men.
verses.32: Men of Ninev will stand trial along with this generation, and they will be judged accordingly. They have neglected to listen to Jonah’s message. And indeed, Jonah is more important than them.
verses.33: No one placed the urn in a container for storage; instead, they placed it right on top of the urn itself, so that those who searched would be able to see the ashes.
verses.34: Your body’s “tomb” is your eyes. When your eyes are healthy, your entire body becomes illuminated. But when they are damaged, your body becomes darkened.
verses.35: Therefore, it aims not to make the light that is in you darkness.
verses.36: So, if your body is completely illuminated, with no part being dark, then it will remain illuminated just as when the lamp shines on you.
verses.37: While he was speaking, a Pharisee tried to praise him in front of him. But when he stepped forward, he fell down.
verses.38: But the Pharisee, seeing this, was astonished that he had not baptized first before the great occasion.
verses.39: And the Lord said to them, “Now, you Pharisees, you clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but inside it, you fill it with robbery and evil.
verses.40: Wicked ones, did they not create what was outside as well as what was inside?
verses.41: In addition to giving you peace of mind, everything else is also pure for you.
verses.42: But to you, Pharisees, I say that you should also abstain from wearing fine clothes and from eating meat, as well as from all kinds of forbidden foods. Also, you should abstain from judging others and from showing favoritism toward anyone. These things must be done, and they should not be ignored.
verses.43: And to you, Pharisees, I say, that you love the chief seats in the synagogues and the praises in the markets.
verses.44: And to you, it’s like those unmarked memorials; the people who traveled above them didn’t know about them at all.
verses.45: Then someone from the legal team said to him, “Teacher, by saying such things, you are only causing us trouble.”
verses.46: He said, “And it’s not right for you, the lawyers, to impose excessive burdens on people. You also don’t compensate those who are responsible for paying these taxes.”
verses.47: And know this: You build monuments to the prophets, but your fathers destroyed them.
verses.48: Therefore, you also serve as witnesses and evidence for the deeds of your fathers. They destroyed them, while you are building houses for yourselves.
verses.49: Therefore, God said, “I will send prophets and messengers to them. From among them, they will be destroyed and driven away.”
verses.50: So that the blood of all the prophets may be cleansed from that which has been scattered from this world, from this generation.
verses.51: From the blood of Abel down to the blood of Zacharias, who was killed between the altar and the house. I say, they will be punished by their own family for this.
verses.52: And to you, the legal experts, it is said that you have denied the right to knowledge. They did not allow those who wanted to enter to do so, and they also rejected those who tried to enter.
verses.53: As soon as he left that place, the officials and the Pharisees began to urge him vehemently to give up his beliefs.
verses.54: They were also causing some kind of damage from his mouth.
